summary.text: Jeremy Orchard is the Labour DLP candidate for Werribee at the 2026 Victorian state election, on the VEC's list of nominations. Neither the ABC nor the party had published a biography of him as at 9 Nov 2026, and the party's website was not serving any pages when checked.

summary.text: John Lister is the Labor MP for Werribee, elected at the February 2025 by-election held after Tim Pallas resigned. He was an English teacher at Wyndham Central College and earlier a ministerial adviser, and is a CFA volunteer in Werribee. He is standing for Werribee again at the 2026 election.

prior_roles.note: Wikipedia says he taught there before his election; no start year given.

summary.text: Matt Emerson is the Family First candidate for Werribee at the 2026 Victorian election. His background is in business operations across telecommunications, media and IT, in both government enterprises and small firms. This is his fourth run for Family First, after Werribee in 2022, the 2025 Werribee by-election and the federal seat of Lalor in 2025.

occupation.text: Business operations in telecommunications, media and IT

priorities.text: Giving parents the main say over their children's schooling and welfare
Opposes abortion on demand and euthanasia

summary.text: Monica Sharma Raizada, listed by the ABC as Monica Raizada, is standing as an independent for Werribee at the 2026 Victorian state election, on the VEC's list of nominations. The ABC's guide links to a Facebook page for them but gives no biography. A candidate of the same name stood as an Independent Labor candidate for Iramoo Ward on Wyndham City Council in 2024 and was not elected.

summary.text: Paul Hopper is The West Party's candidate for Werribee at the 2026 Victorian election; he founded the party in 2025. A lifelong Werribee local, he owns a group of car dealerships across Melbourne's western and south-western suburbs. He stood as an independent at the 2022 state election and at the 2025 by-election, where he polled 14.6 per cent of first preferences.

occupation.text: Runs a chain of car dealerships

priorities.text: Local representation for Werribee, through a party that runs candidates only in Melbourne's west
Under the party model he founded, each candidate settles local policies after consulting the community

summary.text: Paul Pateras is the One Nation candidate for Werribee at the 2026 Victorian election. The ABC's election guide says he is a Werribee-born small business owner whose work is in security contracting. Neither the ABC nor any other source we could read had published more about him by November 2026.

sources.title: Werribee: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News

summary.text: Reece Clark is the Liberal candidate for Werribee at the 2026 Victorian election. The ABC's guide describes him as a lifelong local and says he has worked as a security guard and a project manager. His Liberal Party candidate page could not be read for this profile.

sources.title: Werribee, Victorian election 2026 guide, ABC News

summary.text: Sandhya Kayagurla is the candidate of The Republican, a party registered in Victoria, for Werribee at the 2026 Victorian election. The ABC guide and the Victorian Electoral Commission's nominations list record the candidacy; no biography has been published.

summary.text: Sue Munro is the Victorian Socialists candidate for Werribee at the 2026 Victorian election, having also contested the seat in 2022 and at the 2025 by-election. She is a nurse in the public hospital system and says she has lived in the Werribee and Hoppers Crossing area for about 20 years. At the 2025 by-election she polled 7.1 per cent of first preferences.

prior_roles.role: Community campaigner (disability access, public housing, anti-racism)

priorities.text: Werribee needs public housing to be expanded.
Werribee needs permanently free public transport and improved bus reliability.
Better access to health care, including mental health services, and services for new housing estates
Responses to crime that deal with poverty instead of relying on prison

sources.title: Werribee: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Sue Munro, Victorian Socialists
2025 Werribee state by-election, Wikipedia

summary.text: Tushar Kumar is the Greens candidate for Werribee at the 2026 Victorian election. Originally from India, he is an IT professional who has held project management and product roles at the ANZ bank since 2013. His campaign focuses on public transport, housing and climate action in Melbourne's west.

occupation.text: IT project manager and product owner

priorities.text: I'm a migrant and IT professional
Better public transport and affordable housing for the western suburbs
Infrastructure built to withstand a changing climate
Investment in schools, anti-racism work and community wellbeing

Tushar Kumar, Candidate for Werribee, Victorian Greens
